title: Find what is filling a disk

MOUNT.means: the full filesystem's mount point, e.g. /var

steps.say: Which filesystem is full: Use% near 100.
If space is left but IUse% is 100, the disk is full of small files, not big ones.
Biggest folders on that filesystem. Repeat one level further down the biggest.
Big single files on that filesystem.
Deleted files still held open: their space returns only when that process restarts.
Space used by the system journal.
If the journal is big: delete the oldest logs until it is under 500 MB.
Remove downloaded package files (.deb) from apt's cache.
steps.rollback: Nothing to undo: apt downloads them again when needed.

pitfalls: Don't delete files in /var/lib or /var/lib/dpkg to make space: the system needs them.
Emptying a log that a process writes to (instead of deleting it) frees space at once: sudo truncate -s 0 FILE
